title: Large shell output dumps can become circular and unrecoverable
wanted_capability: When shell output exceeds inline limits, the harness should preserve a bounded diagnostic tail and exit status without requiring agents to chase dump files that reference other dumps.
missing_primitive: Robust shell output capture/dump tail for large compile output
fallback_used: Use shell_run/shell_poll/shell_kill `output_filter` for known noisy command streams; fall back to bounded output caps or recipe-specific command filters only when the needed diagnostic line shape is not yet known.
notes: Genericized from private Java refactor probes. Probe 4 confirmed the tension: the bare compile preserved exit status but dumped large generated-code noise; the agent then used a piped/head command to reduce output, violating protocol. Implemented a host-side `output_filter` on shell_run/shell_poll/shell_kill that keeps matching stdout/stderr lines after capture, preserves the primary command exit_code, persists across polls, and can be explicitly cleared with an empty filter. Remaining unresolved scope: automatic bounded diagnostic tail / recovery for output lost at the in-memory buffer cap is still not solved.
